headline: After Thursday's −2.9% AI rout, NQ is only −0.3% pre-open inside a tight overnight range. Oil at $101/$114 and flash PMI at 9:45 cut both ways. Wait for a break of the overnight range.
session_note: Cash open 9:30 AM ET (10:30 AM Atlantic) · morning window

flip.long: NQ breaks and holds above the overnight high (29,274; ≈ NDX 29,091) after 9:30, with chips (MU/AMD/NVDA) holding their premarket bounce and the 10-year staying under ~5.00%.
flip.short: NQ breaks the overnight low (29,022.75; ≈ NDX 28,840), which also puts cash NDX below Thursday's 28,855 low. Short failed retests, especially if WTI pushes further above $101 or the 9:45 PMIs run hot.

thesis: There's no clear edge at the open. Thursday's AI selloff took the NDX down 2.9% to 28,958.69 (low 28,855.10) after Meta fell ~7–8% on its capex plans and AMD and Nvidia dropped 8% and 4.4% [1,3]. Overnight, Nasdaq-100 futures are only modestly lower at ~29,062–29,070 (−0.25 to −0.27%, 8:32–8:40 AM ET), trading inside a narrow 29,022.75–29,274.00 range [2,4]. Chips and neoclouds are bouncing premarket (AMD and Micron ~+1%), while Meta is −0.6% and telecoms are −4–5% on the SpaceX wireless report [3,5,6]. The headwinds are oil and rates. WTI is ~$101 (+1.7%) and Brent ~$114–115 on reports of renewed US/Israeli strikes on Iran [4,6]. The 10-year has ticked up ~2 bp to ~4.976% after Thursday's biggest one-day drop since March 2023 [5,7]. Fed pricing has edged hawkish: October hike odds are 13.8% (8.0% a day ago), and **Dec: 69% for one hike, 10.5% for two** [8]. No data came out before the open. The **9:45 AM flash PMIs** and the 10:00 AM final UMich sentiment arrive inside the first 30 minutes [9,10]. With futures implying a cash open near ~28,880 (just above Thursday's 28,855 low) and catalysts that point both ways, the call is **stand aside until the overnight range breaks**.
evidence_cutoff: Fri Oct 23, 2026, 8:49 AM ET (9:49 AM Atlantic). Latest futures quotes: 8:32 AM ET (Markets Insider), 8:40 AM ET (Yahoo, may be delayed).

bullets.label: The rout is pausing, not reversing.
bullets.text: NDX fell 2.9% Thursday, its worst day since June, after Meta (~−7–8%) reported its first cash outflow in more than a decade on AI spending. AMD fell ~8% and Nvidia 4.4% [1,3,5]. Premarket, NQ is only −0.25 to −0.3%, and Reuters says Mag 7 names are 'little changed' [2,3,4].

bullets.label: Tight overnight range = no gap edge.
bullets.text: NQ has traded 29,022.75–29,274.00 (~250 pts) against a 29,142 settle [2]. On a ~183-pt futures premium, that implies a cash open near ~28,880, right on top of Thursday's 28,855 low [1,2]. That's an estimate, not a quote.

bullets.label: Catalysts inside the first 30 minutes.
bullets.text: S&P Global flash PMIs at 9:45 AM ET (consensus mfg 55.4, services 57.9) and final UMich sentiment at 10:00 AM (consensus 46.3, 1-yr inflation expectations 4.7%) [9,10]. No 8:30 data and no Fed speakers. The FOMC meets Oct 27–28 [9,11].

bullets.label: Macro tilt is mildly negative.
bullets.text: WTI is above $101 and Brent ~$114.9 on Iran strike reports. The 10-year is up ~2 bp to ~4.976%, and October hike odds rose to 13.8% from 8.0% [4,6,7,8]. Against that, chips are bouncing premarket and the 10-year is still below 5% after Thursday's big rally [5,7].

bullets.label: Bull case:
bullets.text: After a −2.9% day, futures are barely lower and chips/neoclouds are bouncing (AMD and Micron ~+1%, SK Hynix rebounding). The 10-year is near 4.97% after its biggest one-day drop since March 2023, and the WSJ says early trade suggests the AI rout 'could find a floor for now' [3,5,6,12]. A hold of Thursday's low could spark a Friday short-covering bounce toward 29,187 (last Friday's close) [1].

bullets.label: Bear case:
bullets.text: The AI-capex/financing story hasn't been resolved (Jensen Huang: 'scarcity of capital'), and Microsoft/Alphabet/Amazon don't report until next week. Oil above $100 with Iran escalation risk keeps December hike pricing firm. A cash open near Thursday's low that fails could become a breakdown into the weekend [3,6,8].

bullets.label: Flip to LONG:
bullets.text: NQ breaks and holds above the overnight high (29,274; ≈ NDX 29,091) through the first 30 min, ideally with a soft/in-line flash PMI, the 10-year back under ~4.95%, and SMH holding its premarket bounce.

bullets.label: Flip to SHORT:
bullets.text: NQ breaks the overnight low (29,022.75), so cash NDX trades below Thursday's 28,855 low. Stronger if WTI extends above ~$102, the PMIs or UMich inflation expectations run hot, or the 10-year pushes back above 5.00%.

bullets.label: Wildcards:
bullets.text: US/Israel–Iran headlines, SpaceX wireless/telecom news, AI-financing or neocloud credit headlines, and any pre-blackout Fed leak ahead of the Oct 28 decision [3,4,6,11].

data_notes: NQ quotes are indicative (Markets Insider is from market makers; Yahoo may be delayed ~10 min). The overnight range comes from Yahoo's Oct 23 daily bar as of 8:40 AM ET and may have changed since. The implied NDX open uses Thursday's ~183-pt premium (NQ settle 29,142 vs NDX close 28,958.69) and is an estimate. The 10-year is ~4.97–4.976% across CNBC and Yahoo (+1 to +2 bp). Fed odds differ by source: Investing.com shows 13.8% for an October hike (8:15 AM ET), CME FedWatch via GMT Eight shows 7.2%, and a FedWatch-method mirror shows 12.0% (12:45 UTC). The Investing.com calendar lists PMI/UMich times an hour earlier (8:45/9:00), probably a time-zone display issue; the standard 9:45/10:00 AM ET times are used. No US data was released before the open and no Fed speakers are scheduled. No Nasdaq-100 megacap reports today: overnight reports were Western Digital (beat, −5% AH) and Bloom Energy; before the open, AmEx, HCA, SLB and others (non-NDX). Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report next week.
